personal.name: Dwij Vyas
personal.role: Electronics & Communication Engineering — Embedded Systems, Robotics & Applied AI
personal.summary: I'm an Electronics & Communication Engineering undergraduate at BVM, working across embedded systems, digital electronics and applied AI. My work spans hardware design, firmware and the software that ties them together. I'm looking for an internship where I can do this kind of work on a real team.
personal.heroSub: Dwij Vyas — Electronics & Communication Engineering at BVM, building embedded systems, robotics and applied AI.

approach.heading: Discrete logic, worn breadboards, one bus left open.
approach.lead: My work begins where the datasheet stops. A rescue robot that flies to a site and then drives into it. A processor with no microcode to hide behind. Every design earns its place on a breadboard first, because that is where an idea meets the tolerances it has to live with.
approach.body: I design the hardware, write the firmware, and build the software that binds them — schematic, PCB, enclosure, autonomy stack. Nothing here stopped at simulation. Every system on this page was fabricated, debugged, and made to run.

personal.closing: I'm looking for an internship where this work continues on a real team — hardware design, firmware, and the software that binds them. I do my best work close to the bench, with a board in front of me and a problem that has not been solved yet.

projects.title: TerraAvis
projects.summary: Flies to the site, then drives into it. Thermal imaging, FPV and real-time object detection on board.
projects.lead: An AI-enabled hybrid rescue robot with a dual-mode mobility system: aerial navigation to reach the site, tracked ground movement to work inside it.
projects.body: Thermal imaging, FPV surveillance, real-time object detection and autonomous control, built for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Airframe, board, autonomy stack and ground station were designed together rather than bolted on.
projects.hard: Handing control between two vehicles that share one airframe — the transition from flight to tracked ground movement.

projects.title: 4-Bit Microprocessor
projects.summary: A complete datapath — ALU, registers, program counter, shared bus — under a hardwired control unit.
projects.lead: A fully functional 4-bit microprocessor built entirely from discrete 74-series logic ICs on breadboards.
projects.body: A complete datapath — ALU, registers, instruction register, program counter and a shared bus — driven by a hardwired control unit, with a custom instruction set covering arithmetic, logical, load, store and conditional jump operations.
projects.hard: A hardwired control unit: every micro-operation timed by hand, with no microcode to hide behind.

projects.title: Friendly AI Chatbot
projects.summary: An ESP32 that listens and answers. Custom PCB, printed enclosure, conversation loop in Python.
projects.lead: A standalone embedded AI device built around an ESP32: real-time voice input, amplified audio output, and an OLED display for feedback.
projects.body: The board was drawn in EasyEDA and the enclosure printed from a Fusion 360 model; Python drives the conversational logic. It runs on its own, with no phone and no laptop in the loop.
projects.hard: Real-time voice in and amplified audio out on a microcontroller — with the whole conversation loop fitting the board.

projects.title: Dual-Axis CNC Plotter
projects.summary: G-code in, ink on paper out. Motion-control firmware and a frame built to hold its tolerance.
projects.lead: A 2-axis CNC plotter: Arduino, stepper motors and a custom mechanical frame that turn digital designs into precise physical drawings.
projects.body: G-code interpretation and motion-control firmware handle pen positioning; the frame was designed to hold its tolerance while the head moves. Embedded systems and mechanical design in the same object.
projects.hard: Motion control accurate enough that the pen lands where the G-code says it will — backlash included.

projects.title: DoseGuard
projects.kind: AI systems · Nuclear science · Interactive data
projects.summary: A gamma-irradiation decision engine grounded in 30+ IAEA papers and each destination country's limits.
projects.lead: A standards-grounded decision engine for gamma irradiation, built on 30+ IAEA research papers and cross-referenced against each destination country's own regulatory limits.
projects.body: Checked against limits such as FDA 21 CFR 179.26, it generates a downloadable prescription report with recommendations tailored to a specific product and facility. Built for HackAtom Summer University 2026 at Ural Federal University.
projects.hard: Turning 30+ IAEA papers and per-country regulatory limits into one engine whose output a regulator would accept.

experience.body: Wrote production firmware in C on the AVR128DA48 for Modsonic's ultrasonic thickness gauges. Migrated the display and keypad interface to an SPI TFT with capacitive touch, and developed the IC LCD driver for the next generation of the instrument.

Selected for URFU's Summer University programme, where I led the HackAtom team that built DoseGuard — a regulatory decision engine for gamma irradiation. Four weeks of designing, prototyping and defending technical work alongside international teams.

recognition.body: TerraAvis, the hybrid aerial-and-tracked rescue robot, advanced through the state rounds to the Gujarat finals.
